merger_description:
Adbri Pty Ltd (**Adbri**) proposes to acquire the business of Eureka Concrete (Holdings) Pty Ltd (**Eureka**), including its ready-mix concrete (**RMX**) operations, quarry assets, plant and equipment, motor vehicles, certain freehold properties, intellectual property, and associated business contracts, together with the transfer of employees.

Adbri supplies cement, RMX and aggregates nationally, including through E.B. Mawson & Sons Pty Ltd (**Mawsons**), Central Pre-Mix Concrete Pty Ltd and Hy-Tec Industries (Victoria) Pty Ltd.

Mawsons is an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of Adbri. Mawsons supplies RMX, quarry products and landscaping products throughout northern and central regional Victoria, and southern regional NSW, including through Lake Boga Quarries Pty Ltd.

Eureka supplies RMX and sand quarry products in the areas surrounding Ballarat. The business operates 4 concrete batch plants in Ballarat, Beaufort, Ballan and Maryborough and a sand quarry in Amphitheatre.

determination_table_content.details:
Adbri Pty Ltd (Adbri) proposes to acquire the business of Eureka
Concrete (Holdings) Pty Ltd (Eureka)(together, the Parties),
including its ready-mix concrete (RMX) operations, quarry assets,
plant and equipment, motor vehicles, certain freehold properties,
intellectual property, and associated business contracts, together
with the transfer of employees (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Adbri, supplies cement, RMX and aggregates
nationally, including through E.B Mawson & Sons Pty Ltd, Central
Pre-Mix Concrete Pty Ltd and Hy-Tec Industries (Victoria) Pty Ltd.
The target, Eureka, is a supplier of RMX and sand quarry products in
Victoria, operating 4 concrete batch plants located in Ballarat,
Beaufort, Ballan and Maryborough and a sand quarry in
Amphitheatre.

The Parties overlap in the supply of RMX and sand quarry products
in Victoria.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and prior relevant merger assessments.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
• The Acquisition would not result in a material increase in
Adbri’s share of supply in RMX in any relevant overlapping
geographic area.
• Adbri would continue to compete with many alternative
suppliers of RMX in each overlapping geographic area.
• The Parties do not supply quarry products in overlapping
geographic areas.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
